---
title: "Integrated embedding of the song / non-song glutamatergic datasets (hybrid labels)"
format:
  html:
    toc: true
    df-print: paged
---

The integration in `snrna/integration/song_nonsong_integration_hybrid.qmd` does produce a
common reduction -- `IntegrateData()` returns a corrected `integrated` assay and that
notebook runs a PCA on it -- but it uses that space only to count each song cell's nearest
non-song neighbours, then discards the object. Nothing was saved, so there was no embedding
to look at.

This notebook regenerates the integration for the requested setting (**`k.anchor = 20`,
CCA**), runs a UMAP on the common PCA, and saves the coordinates. For reference it also
embeds the same cells **without** integration, from a PCA on the merged uncorrected SCT data,
since an integrated UMAP is hard to read without knowing what it started from.

**Embedding parameters.** PCA on the integrated assay, `npcs = 30`; UMAP on
`dims = 1:30` with Seurat's defaults throughout -- `n.neighbors = 30`, `min.dist = 0.3`,
`metric = "cosine"`, `spread = 1`, `n.components = 2`, `umap.method = "uwot"`,
`seed.use = 42`. Nothing is tuned. Those defaults are deliberately smoothing: `min.dist`
of 0.3 with 30 neighbours will show a cluster split into lobes whenever some
consistent sub-structure exists, without that split meaning the cells are separate types.

A caution about reading it. The integration removes the dataset-level (song vs non-song)
offset, so the two datasets will overlap more after correction by construction -- that is
what was asked of it, not evidence of anything. The interpretable part is *which* non-song
cell type each song type ends up adjacent to, which is the quantity the anchor and neighbour
tabulations measure directly and with a null behind them. Treat this embedding as a picture
of that result rather than as the evidence for it.

```{r setup}
#| message: false
library(Seurat)
library(tidyverse)
library(qs2)
library(here)
set.seed(10)

knitr::opts_chunk$set(dev = "ragg_png", dpi = 200)

source(here::here("config/figure_theme.R"))
source(file.path(Sys.getenv("COLQUITTLAB_UTILS", "/opt/colquittlab/utils"), "R", "common_aesthetics.R"))

options(future.globals.maxSize = Inf)
```

# Parameters

```{r params}
sets        = c("ARCO", "NIDO", "ALL")
reduction   = "cca"
k_anchor    = 20
dims_to_use = 1:30
norm_method = "SCT"

song_pattern = "HVC|LMAN|-RA$"

parent_dir = here::here("snrna/integration/song_nonsong_integration_hybrid")
cache_dir  = file.path(parent_dir, "cache")

## Read-only, for the per-cell individual id, which the cached preps do not carry
obj_fname = here::here("snrna/trees/celltypes_hclust_glut_robustness_hybrid",
                       "obj_clustered_glutamatergic.qs2")

script_name = "song_nonsong_umap_hybrid"
out_dir   = here::here("snrna/integration", script_name)
umap_cache = file.path(out_dir, "cache")
dir.create(umap_cache, recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)

n_threads = min(16L, max(1L, parallel::detectCores() - 4L))
RhpcBLASctl::blas_set_num_threads(n_threads)
RcppParallel::setThreadOptions(numThreads = n_threads)
```

# Embed

The per-dataset SCTransform fits are reused from the parent notebook's cache, so only the
anchor-finding, correction and embedding are recomputed here.

```{r embed}
#| message: false
embed_one = function(set_name) {
  f = file.path(umap_cache, sprintf("umap_%s_%s_k%02d.qs2", set_name, reduction, k_anchor))
  if (file.exists(f)) return(qs_read(f))
  message("== ", set_name)

  prep = qs_read(file.path(cache_dir, sprintf("prep_%s.qs2", set_name)), nthreads = 8)
  lab  = prep$labels

  ## --- uncorrected reference: the two datasets merged, no anchors ----------
  mg = merge(prep$list[[1]], prep$list[[2]])
  DefaultAssay(mg) = "SCT"
  VariableFeatures(mg) = prep$features
  mg = mg %>%
    ScaleData(features = prep$features, verbose = FALSE) %>%
    RunPCA(features = prep$features, npcs = max(dims_to_use), verbose = FALSE) %>%
    RunUMAP(dims = dims_to_use, verbose = FALSE)
  umap_raw = as.data.frame(Embeddings(mg, "umap")) %>%
    rownames_to_column("cell") %>%
    setNames(c("cell", "umap_1", "umap_2")) %>%
    mutate(embedding = "uncorrected")
  rm(mg); gc()

  ## --- integrated ----------------------------------------------------------
  anchors = FindIntegrationAnchors(prep$list, anchor.features = prep$features,
                                   normalization.method = norm_method,
                                   reduction = reduction, dims = dims_to_use,
                                   k.anchor = k_anchor, verbose = FALSE)
  k_weight = min(100, min(vapply(prep$list, ncol, integer(1))) - 1)
  int = IntegrateData(anchorset = anchors, normalization.method = norm_method,
                      dims = dims_to_use, k.weight = k_weight, verbose = FALSE)
  DefaultAssay(int) = "integrated"
  int = int %>%
    RunPCA(npcs = max(dims_to_use), verbose = FALSE) %>%
    RunUMAP(dims = dims_to_use, verbose = FALSE)
  umap_int = as.data.frame(Embeddings(int, "umap")) %>%
    rownames_to_column("cell") %>%
    setNames(c("cell", "umap_1", "umap_2")) %>%
    mutate(embedding = "integrated")

  res = bind_rows(umap_raw, umap_int) %>%
    mutate(set = set_name,
           label = unname(lab[cell]),
           dataset = if_else(grepl(song_pattern, label), "song", "non-song"),
           library = unname(prep$libs[cell]))
  qs_save(res, f, nthreads = 4)
  rm(int, anchors); gc()
  res
}

## Per-cell individual (souporcell `assignment`). Cached as a small table so the
## multi-GB object is read once.
##
## IMPORTANT: `assignment` indexes birds WITHIN a library and is not comparable
## across libraries -- assignment 0 in ra_run1 is a different bird from
## assignment 0 in arco_run1. Any figure coloured by it therefore has to be read
## within a library, which is why the panels below facet on library rather than
## pooling the three colours across all of them.
ind_fname = file.path(umap_cache, "cell_individual.qs2")
if (file.exists(ind_fname)) {
  individuals = qs_read(ind_fname)
} else {
  o = qs_read(obj_fname, nthreads = 8)
  individuals = tibble(cell = colnames(o),
                       assignment = as.character(o$assignment),
                       individual = paste(o$sample_name, o$assignment, sep = "_"))
  qs_save(individuals, ind_fname, nthreads = 4)
  rm(o); gc()
}

umap = map_dfr(sets, embed_one) %>%
  mutate(embedding = factor(embedding, levels = c("uncorrected", "integrated"))) %>%
  left_join(individuals, by = "cell")
write_csv(umap, file.path(out_dir, "umap_coordinates.csv.gz"))
count(umap, set, embedding, dataset)
```

# Figures

```{r fig-fns}
## Song types drop the division prefix (they are identified by nucleus); non-song
## types keep it in abbreviated form, since a bare number would not say which
## division a partner belongs to.
short = function(x) {
  if_else(grepl(song_pattern, x),
          str_replace(x, "^Glut-(DACH2|CACNA1H)-", ""),
          x %>%
            str_replace("^Glut-DACH2-", "D2-") %>%
            str_replace("^Glut-CACNA1H-", "C1H-") %>%
            str_replace("^Glut-", ""))
}

song_position = function(x) case_when(grepl("LMAN", x) ~ "lman",
                                      grepl("HVC", x)  ~ "hvc",
                                      grepl("RA", x)   ~ "ra",
                                      TRUE             ~ NA_character_)

## Song types in the standard position colours, every non-song type in grey.
## Identity is carried by the direct labels at each type's centroid, not by the
## colour alone -- with a dozen types no categorical palette would separate them.
type_colour = function(labels) {
  u = unique(labels)
  cols = if_else(grepl(song_pattern, u),
                 unname(position_colors[song_position(u)]),
                 FIG_INK_MUTED)
  setNames(cols, u)
}

## Points are rasterised and everything else stays vector: these panels carry
## thousands of cells each, and a fully vector UMAP makes an unwieldy PDF that
## some layout programs choke on. Text, axes and tiles remain editable.
raster_points = function(...) ggrastr::rasterise(geom_point(...), dpi = 600, dev = "ragg")

centroids = function(d) {
  d %>% group_by(label) %>%
    summarise(umap_1 = median(umap_1), umap_2 = median(umap_2), .groups = "drop") %>%
    mutate(lab = short(label))
}
```

```{r fig-umap-type}
#| fig-width: 5
#| fig-height: 2.6
#| results: hold
## Panels are pinned to a fixed physical size rather than the page being sized:
## these are destined for a composed figure, where what has to be exact is the
## panel, not the margins around it.
panel_in = 1.4

## `label_which`: "all" labels every type; "song" labels only the song nuclei,
## which is what fits once the panel is down at 1.4 in with 17 types in it.
## `bare` strips the titles, axis titles and legend for drop-in use in a layout.
umap_plot = function(d, ttl, label_which = "all", bare = FALSE) {
  cols = type_colour(unique(d$label))
  lab_d = d %>% group_by(embedding) %>% group_modify(~ centroids(.x)) %>% ungroup()
  if (label_which == "song") lab_d = filter(lab_d, grepl(song_pattern, label))

  p = ggplot(d, aes(umap_1, umap_2)) +
    raster_points(aes(colour = label), size = 0.12, stroke = 0, alpha = 0.55,
                  show.legend = FALSE) +
    ggrepel::geom_text_repel(data = lab_d, aes(label = lab), size = fig_pt(5), family = FIG_FONT,
                             colour = FIG_INK_PRIMARY, segment.size = 0.15,
                             segment.colour = FIG_INK_MUTED, min.segment.length = 0.1,
                             max.overlaps = Inf, box.padding = 0.1, seed = 1) +
    facet_wrap(~embedding, nrow = 1) +
    scale_colour_manual(values = cols) +
    scale_x_continuous(expand = fig_expand()) +
    scale_y_continuous(expand = fig_expand()) +
    theme_fig() +
    theme(panel.grid.major = element_blank(),
          panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
          axis.text = element_blank(),
          axis.ticks = element_blank(),
          strip.text = element_text(size = FIG_PT_AXIS_TITLE, colour = FIG_INK_SECONDARY))

  p = if (bare) {
    p + labs(x = NULL, y = NULL) +
      theme(strip.text = element_blank(), plot.margin = margin(1, 1, 1, 1))
  } else {
    p + labs(x = "UMAP 1", y = "UMAP 2", title = ttl,
             subtitle = sprintf("%s, k.anchor = %d | song types coloured, non-song grey",
                                toupper(reduction), k_anchor))
  }
  egg::set_panel_size(p, width = unit(panel_in, "in"), height = unit(panel_in, "in"))
}

## Writes PDF, PNG and SVG from one call.
##
## The SVG exists because of how cairo_pdf emits text: it coalesces consecutive
## labels sharing a font into a single BT...ET block, moving between them with
## Td, so Illustrator imports several labels as ONE text object. svglite writes
## one <text> element per label, which imports as separate, editable text boxes.
## Use the SVG for figure assembly and the PDF for the record.
fig_save_gt = function(gt, path_noext, dpi = 600) {
  fig_check_font()
  w = grid::convertWidth(sum(gt$widths), "in", valueOnly = TRUE)
  h = grid::convertHeight(sum(gt$heights), "in", valueOnly = TRUE)
  ggsave(paste0(path_noext, ".pdf"), gt, width = w, height = h,
         device = cairo_pdf, family = FIG_FONT)
  ## ragg's default family is "sans"; name Arial explicitly so the PNG matches
  ## the PDF for any text that does not carry its own family
  ggsave(paste0(path_noext, ".png"), gt, width = w, height = h, dpi = dpi,
         bg = FIG_SURFACE, device = ragg::agg_png)
  ggsave(paste0(path_noext, ".svg"), gt, width = w, height = h,
         device = svglite::svglite, bg = FIG_SURFACE)
  invisible(paste0(path_noext, c(".pdf", ".png", ".svg")))
}

for (st in sets) {
  d = filter(umap, set == st)
  gt = umap_plot(d, sprintf("%s glutamatergic types", st))
  plot(gt)
  fig_save_gt(gt, file.path(out_dir, sprintf("umap_%s_by_type", tolower(st))))
  ## drop-in variants for a composed figure: song labels only, and no chrome
  fig_save_gt(umap_plot(d, NULL, label_which = "song"),
              file.path(out_dir, sprintf("umap_%s_by_type_songlabels", tolower(st))))
  fig_save_gt(umap_plot(d, NULL, label_which = "song", bare = TRUE),
              file.path(out_dir, sprintf("umap_%s_by_type_bare", tolower(st))))
}
```

```{r fig-umap-dataset}
#| fig-width: 6
#| fig-height: 3.2
#| results: hold
## The same embeddings coloured by dataset, which is what the integration acted
## on: it should pull the two together between the left and right panels.
for (st in sets) {
  d = filter(umap, set == st)
  p = ggplot(d, aes(umap_1, umap_2, colour = dataset)) +
    raster_points(size = 0.12, stroke = 0, alpha = 0.55) +
    facet_wrap(~embedding, nrow = 1) +
    scale_colour_manual(values = c(song = FIG_PAL[2], `non-song` = FIG_INK_MUTED),
                        name = NULL) +
    scale_x_continuous(expand = fig_expand()) +
    scale_y_continuous(expand = fig_expand()) +
    guides(colour = guide_legend(override.aes = list(size = 1.2, alpha = 1))) +
    labs(x = "UMAP 1", y = "UMAP 2", title = sprintf("%s, by dataset", st),
         subtitle = sprintf("%s, k.anchor = %d", toupper(reduction), k_anchor)) +
    theme_fig() +
    ## theme_fig() sets panel.grid.major explicitly, and a specific element
    ## beats the panel.grid parent, so both children have to be blanked
    theme(panel.grid.major = element_blank(),
          panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
          axis.text = element_blank(),
          axis.ticks = element_blank(),
          strip.text = element_text(size = FIG_PT_AXIS_TITLE, colour = FIG_INK_SECONDARY))
  print(p)
  fig_save(p, file.path(out_dir, sprintf("umap_%s_by_dataset", tolower(st))),
           width = 5.2, height = 2.6)
}
```

```{r fig-umap-assignment}
#| fig-width: 7
#| fig-height: 3.4
#| results: hold
## Coloured by individual bird. Faceted by library because `assignment` only
## identifies a bird within its own library; the same three colours in two
## different library panels are six different birds.
##
## This is the panel to check when a cluster looks split: if the lobes separate
## by colour within a library panel, the split is inter-individual rather than
## a cell-type distinction.
for (st in sets) {
  ## libraries contributing only a handful of cells to this analysis would take a
  ## full panel to show nothing (ARCO has one lman cell), so drop them
  keep_lib = umap %>% filter(set == st) %>% count(library) %>%
    filter(n >= 20 * 2) %>% pull(library)   # x2: each cell appears in both embeddings
  d = filter(umap, set == st, library %in% keep_lib)
  p = ggplot(d, aes(umap_1, umap_2, colour = assignment)) +
    raster_points(size = 0.3, stroke = 0, alpha = 0.75) +
    facet_grid(embedding ~ library) +
    scale_colour_manual(values = setNames(FIG_PAL[1:3], c("0", "1", "2")),
                        name = "bird (within library)") +
    scale_x_continuous(expand = fig_expand()) +
    scale_y_continuous(expand = fig_expand()) +
    guides(colour = guide_legend(override.aes = list(size = 1.2, alpha = 1))) +
    labs(x = "UMAP 1", y = "UMAP 2",
         title = sprintf("%s, by individual", st),
         subtitle = sprintf("%s, k.anchor = %d\nassignment indexes birds within a library: the same colour in two panels is two different birds",
                            toupper(reduction), k_anchor)) +
    theme_fig() +
    theme(panel.grid.major = element_blank(),
          panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
          axis.text = element_blank(),
          axis.ticks = element_blank(),
          strip.text = element_text(size = FIG_PT_AXIS_TITLE, colour = FIG_INK_SECONDARY))
  print(p)
  fig_save(p, file.path(out_dir, sprintf("umap_%s_by_individual", tolower(st))),
           width = 1.3 + 1.35 * length(keep_lib), height = 3.2)
}
```

```{r individual-mixing}
## How much of each cell type's spread is between birds? For every type, the
## share of its cells contributed by each bird of each library -- a type whose
## cells come overwhelmingly from one bird is a type whose apparent structure
## could be individual variation.
ind_share = umap %>%
  filter(embedding == "integrated") %>%
  distinct(set, cell, label, library, assignment, individual) %>%
  count(set, label, individual) %>%
  group_by(set, label) %>%
  mutate(share = n / sum(n)) %>%
  slice_max(share, n = 1, with_ties = FALSE) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  rename(top_individual = individual, top_individual_share = share) %>%
  arrange(desc(top_individual_share))
write_csv(ind_share, file.path(out_dir, "top_individual_share_by_type.csv"))
ind_share %>% filter(set != "ALL") %>% mutate(top_individual_share = round(top_individual_share, 3))
```
